findings.issue: The hero's black button sits on the top edge of the tinted trust bar, about 2–4px above it, with no space under it (the same at 390px). The media-banner hero has no bottom padding and counts on the next block's top padding, and that space falls inside the trust bar's tint.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves a clear gap of about 40px or more under its hero buttons ('Request Price', 'Book a Call') before the next section starts.
findings.fix: In template.css give .page-hero[data-variant="media-banner"] .page-hero__inner a bottom padding (e.g. calc(var(--section-space) / 2)) whenever the block after it has its own surface (trust bar, tinted section), so the space sits on the hero's own white ground.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: on phones the check-list item titles ('Exposure and finish', 'Children's safety figures', 'Standalone orders', 'Shipping options') are fitted to about 26px at weight 700. The section headings above them are about 26px at weight 500, so the item level looks as large as the heading or larger. iconList-1, iconList-2 and m10 have the same problem.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps each heading level clearly smaller than the one above: its bold sub-heads sit just above body size under a larger h2.
findings.fix: In the shared heading-fit step, cap an item (h3) heading's fitted size below its section h2's size (e.g. at most ~0.75 of it), so a short item title can no longer grow to the h2's size on phones.

findings.issue: The quote cards are white (--surface-testimonial #ffffff) on a white section, so the card cannot be seen. Its padding shows only as text set about 32px in from the heading's left edge and about 80px below it (about 20px and 70px on phones). The row reads as misaligned text, not as cards.
findings.reference: The competitor's card modules draw their cards as visible outlined boxes. Our own feature cards on this page (m2, m4, m8) follow that with a 1px outline.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give .testimonial the feature cards' outline (border: 1px solid var(--border-color); border-radius as .feature-card) so the card shows on white. Otherwise, set --testimonial-padding: 0 so the quotes start on the content edge.

findings.issue: The related-links section is white directly after the white testimonials section, so two plain sections in a row share one background. Before that point the page alternates white and tint (and does so again with faq after related).
findings.reference: The site rule: neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds, set by the template.
findings.fix: In the template's surface alternation, count the testimonials block (it follows a photo wall) so that related takes the --section-tint surface. Alternatively, start the alternation again after media-module-budget-1 so that testimonials is tinted.

findings.issue: The hero button 'Request a quote for swimwear accessories' breaks onto two lines (a 60px bar). The cta block's button carries the same label, is just as wide, and fits on one line. The hero button wraps only because it keeps the 1.5rem side padding that the cta button drops on phones. The previous review called this a content finding; the cta button shows that the label fits.
findings.reference: The competitor's buttons sit on one line on phones.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css widen the existing phone rule (line 321, .block--cta .cta .button { padding-inline: 1rem; letter-spacing: 0 }) to cover .page-hero__actions .button too, so the hero button keeps to one line like the cta button.

findings.issue: On phones the cost chart's label column takes about 40% of the panel, leaving its two value columns about 75px wide. Values break into stacks of one or two words ('Custom- / moulded, / plus / mould / fee', 'Rose / gold, / gunmetal / or matte / black') and the headers wrap as 'Lower / cost'.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps short figures on one or two lines on phones.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css narrow the chart's label column on phones (e.g. th:first-child { width: 32%; }) and reduce the cell inline padding below 768px, so each value keeps to two lines at most.
